Literal ANVIL FP32 port would mutate gradients: upstream float() copies BF16 gradients, but aliases existing FP32 tensors. The new port uses out-of-place interpolation.
ANVIL BF16 arithmetic requires first-Gram FP32 trace normalization and fused polynomial rounding; new port preserves these boundaries pending numerical verification.
Only matrix LR 0.005 had been freshly benchmarked before this investigation; lower-LR history cases were absent from stored JSON.
Existing gradients have concentrated singular spectra and whitening worsens held-out alignment; weak-mode amplification remains a hypothesis.
ANVIL2 best-run evidence combines optimizer with model and training changes, and does not isolate the optimizer benefit.
